title.en: Preventing hazards and saving lives in minutes

text.en: From handling electrical gadgets and pesticides safely to starting CPR within three minutes of a heart stoppage, knowing basic safety and first aid can save a life.

Prevention is better than cure: concentrate when using machines, switch off power when idle, and never touch moving parts.
Pesticides (insecticides, herbicides, fungicides, rodenticides) are toxic—wash skin immediately with soap and water if sprayed, and keep them away from people with asthma or allergies.
For electrical safety, use ISI-marked appliances, switch off power before and after use, avoid water near wires, and use dry sand (never water) on electrical fires.
First Aid is immediate care before medical help arrives. If a casualty is unconscious and not breathing, start CPR within 3 minutes to prevent brain damage (compressions + artificial breathing).
If a casualty is unconscious but breathing, place them in the recovery position.
Avoid self-medication (taking drugs without medical advice). Substance abuse—non-medical use of drugs/substances—causes organ damage, low immunity, and addiction; life skills and family support help prevent it.
Safety starts with attention: switch off unused machines and never repair electrical gadgets untrained.
In an electrical fire, use dry sand—never water—to put out the flames.
If pesticide splashes on clothes or skin, remove clothes and wash immediately with soap and water.
When someone is unconscious and not breathing, start CPR within 3 minutes to protect the brain.
If someone is unconscious but breathing normally, place them in the recovery position.
Never self-medicate, and resist peer pressure toward substance abuse using life skills.

problem.en: You find someone unconscious after a collapse. They are NOT breathing. What must you do first and within how many minutes?

text.en: Call for medical help and begin CPR (Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation) immediately.
Start within 3 minutes of heart stoppage.

why.en: Brain damage begins if oxygen supply stops for more than 3 minutes.

prompt.en: Explain when to use CPR versus the recovery position, and why self-medication is dangerous.

requiredIdeas.en: Use CPR when unconscious and not breathing (start within 3 minutes)
Use recovery position when unconscious and breathing
Self-medication risks wrong dosage and harmful side effects

commonMisconceptions.en: Throwing water on an electrical fire instead of dry sand

points.en: Use ISI-marked electrical gadgets, switch off power, and use dry sand on electrical fires.
Wash pesticide splashes immediately with soap and water and keep away from food/kitchen.
Start CPR within 3 minutes if unconscious and not breathing; use recovery position if breathing.
Avoid self-medication and substance abuse; seek medical supervision and family support.
